$comment: Committed KNOWN-ORPHAN debt for check:gate-wiring (C-FEL-428).
A gate here is a check:* leaf that is reachable by NEITHER the check:ci
transitive chain NOR an actual run: step in any .github/workflows/*.yml —
so it never runs in CI and can never make a PR red. That is the
FEL-438/FEL-430 green-by-construction shape.
MEASURED, never predicted. check:gate-wiring exits 0 iff the current orphan
set EQUALS this list. A NEW orphan is red and named; a listed orphan that
gets WIRED is ALSO red, forcing the decrement into the same PR as the fix so
the debt cannot silently regrow OR silently shrink. The contract SURFACE
forbids rewiring these gates here — that is separate follow-up work.
Measured 2026-07-28 at origin/main b667bdcd:
- check:hmr (scripts/hmr-check.ts): in no workflow run: step, not in check:ci.
- check:hydration-adoption (scripts/check-hydration-adoption.ts): in no
workflow; its only chain is check:thesis, which is itself invoked by no
workflow — a dead chain.
Re-measured 2026-07-28 at origin/main 642860f3 (C-FEL-GATE-WIRING-RUNS):
- check:grammar-v2 (scripts/check-grammar-v2.ts): NEWLY VISIBLE, not newly
broken. The 'dead chain' reasoning written above for check:thesis is now
applied to check:ci as well, because it is equally true of it — plan-a.yml
says so in its own words, 'check:ci is invoked by no workflow in this
repo'. So this gate's only route was dead and it has never run in CI.
(Compounding it, check:ci misnamed it 'check:grammar-v'; that typo is
fixed, and a dangling `bun run` reference is now red in its own right.)
LISTED HERE RATHER THAN WIRED, against this file's own advice, and the
reason is measured, not a preference. Run it and it is RED on main — but
on FIVE FALSE POSITIVES, every one a COMMENT or a STRING describing a
retired form, none a use of one:
packages/arbor/src/structural.ts:160        doc comment
packages/arbor/tests/structural.test.ts:954 doc comment
packages/cli/src/templates-tooling.ts:135   a warning string telling
users NOT to use those forms
apps/docs/src/data/guide-routing-layouts.ts:4  comment
standalone compiler slot-fallback-drive test describe/it strings
This is the THIRD instance of one class — a regex over raw source cannot
tell CODE from TEXT ABOUT CODE — after #681 (dep-check, comment-blind) and
#689 (check-moon-graph, template-literal-blind). check-grammar-v2 greps
RAW BYTES via `grep -rlE` over whole directories.
It is NOT a copy of #689's fix. stripNonCode() blanks template-literal
contents and PRESERVES ordinary strings; this gate needs the OPPOSITE on
both counts. Ordinary strings are text here (templates-tooling.ts:135),
and a template literal holding .aihu source is exactly the live drift a
GRAMMAR gate must catch. It also greps .aihu and .md files, where a
retired form IS a use. That is per-file-type design judgement, not a
one-line reuse, so it is a separate contract — wiring it on a wrong
stripper either reddens main or blinds the gate.
Baselining is strictly better than the status quo it replaces: the dead
check:ci route made this gate silently 'reachable'; this line prints it as
DEBT on every CI run, and wiring it now forces this line's deletion into
the same PR.
